public_rationale: The search did not establish the two companies' combined share of AI compute sold. Available spending analysis explicitly warns against converting dollars directly into compute capacity. Large purchases or concentrated supplier backlogs cannot establish an industry-wide share without a matching denominator. The missing data prevent either support or contradiction, regardless of the precise cutoff for vast majority.
limitations: The quarter and delivered-services reading are evaluator choices.
The available analysis was published after the post but before the evaluation cutoff.
Two attempted primary prospectus reads failed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of AI compute is sold to either Anthropic or OpenAI.

statement.excerpt: The vast majority of AI compute is sold to either Anthropic or OpenAI.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that the two companies together purchase an overwhelming share of AI compute sold across providers, not merely a narrow majority.
Use July through September 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that public reporting could cover before the post.
Measure compute supplied to the two ultimate purchasers, including purchases through intermediaries, without double counting.
The surrounding backlog discussion is relevant context, but future commitments do not establish the share of compute actually sold during the period.
No geography is specified, so the denominator is worldwide. Internally consumed, unsold compute is outside the sales denominator.
This is a physical compute market-share claim, not a stated revenue or spending figure; metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable industry-wide data show that Anthropic and OpenAI together account for an overwhelming share of AI compute sold in the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable industry-wide data show that other purchasers account for a sufficiently large share to rule out an overwhelming combined share for Anthropic and OpenAI.
